감염·보건.content:
[내외뉴스통신] 이용범 기자
관련사진 [질병관리청 제공]
질병관리청이 겨울철 인플루엔자 유행에 대비해 9월 21일부터 2027년 4월 30일까지 ’26-’27절기 인플루엔자 국가예방접종을 실시한다.
이번 접종은 어린이, 임신부, 어르신을 대상으로 진행되며, 특히 올해부터 학령기 청소년의 유행 확산을 막기 위해 어린이 무료접종 대상이 기존 생후 6개월~13세에서 생후 6개월~14세까지 확대된다.
관련사진 [질병관리청 제공]
접종은 9월 21일 2회 접종 대상 어린이와 임신부를 시작으로, 9월 28일 1회 접종 대상 어린이, 10월 12일 75세 이상 어르신부터 연령대별로 순차 시행된다.
이번 절기에는 세계보건기구(WHO) 권장주가 모두 포함된 3가 인플루엔자 백신을 사용한다.
대상자는 주소지와 관계없이 가까운 위탁의료기관이나 보건소에서 무료로 접종받을 수 있으며, 전국 약 2만3천 개 위탁의료기관은 관할 보건소나 예방접종도우미 누리집에서 확인할 수 있다.
임승관 질병관리청장은 “인플루엔자 예방접종은 입원과 사망을 줄이고 질병 부담을 낮추는 효과적인 수단”이라며 “접종 대상이 14세까지 확대된 만큼 학부모들의 관심과 적극적인 참여를 당부드린다”고 말했다.

감염·보건.content:
/질병관리청 제공
올 겨울 인플루엔자 국가예방접종 지원 대상이 기존 13세 이하에서 14세 이하로 확대된다. 어린이와 임신부를 시작으로 9월 21일부터 접종이 시작되며 65세 이상 어르신은 10월 12일부터 연령대별로 접종받을 수 있다.
질병관리청은 9월 21일부터 내년 4월 30일까지 어린이와 임신부, 65세 이상 어르신을 대상으로 2026~2027절기 인플루엔자 무료 예방접종을 실시한다고 밝혔다.
이번 절기부터 어린이 지원 연령은 생후 6개월~13세에서 생후 6개월~14세로 확대된다. 대상은 2012년 1월 1일부터 2026년 8월 31일까지 출생한 어린이다.
접종은 대상자별로 순차적으로 진행한다.
9월 21일부터는 인플루엔자 백신을 두 차례 맞아야 하는 어린이와 임신부가 접종 대상이다.
2회 접종 대상은 과거 인플루엔자 예방접종을 받은 적이 없거나 기존에 한 차례만 접종한 생후 6개월 이상 9세 미만 어린이다.
2회 접종 대상이 아닌 생후 6개월 이상 14세 이하 어린이는 9월 28일부터 1회 접종을 받을 수 있다.
65세 이상 어르신은 10월 12일 75세 이상부터 접종을 시작한다. 이후 연령대별로 접종 일정이 이어진다.
이번 국가예방접종에는 세계보건기구(WHO)가 권장한 바이러스주가 모두 포함된 3가 인플루엔자 백신을 사용한다.
접종 대상자는 주소지와 관계없이 가까운 위탁의료기관이나 보건소에서 무료로 접종받을 수 있다. 전국 약 2만3천 개 위탁의료기관은 관할 보건소나 예방접종도우미 누리집의 ‘예방접종관리→지정의료기관 찾기’에서 확인할 수 있다.
65세 이상 어르신을 대상으로 한 코로나19 예방접종도 같은 일정으로 진행된다. 질병관리청은 인플루엔자 백신과 코로나19 백신의 동시 접종을 권고하고 있다.
이번 접종 대상 확대는 학령기 아동·청소년의 인플루엔자 유행 확산을 줄이기 위한 조치다. 특히 학교와 학원 등 집단생활이 많은 연령층의 예방접종 참여가 겨울철 유행 규모에 영향을 줄 수 있어 보호자의 관심이 중요하다.
질병관리청은 어린이와 임신부, 어르신의 인플루엔자로 인한 입원과 사망을 줄이고 질병 부담을 낮추기 위해 예방접종 참여가 필요하다고 강조했다.
/오승현 기자 romi0328@namdonews.com

질병관리청은 다음달 21일부터 내년 4월까지 어린이와 임신부, 노인을 대상으로 독감 국가예방접종을 시행한다고 밝혔습니다.
이번 절기 예방접종부터는 현재 중학교 2학년인 14살도 예방접종 대상에 추가돼 무료로 백신을 맞을 수 있습니다.
인플루엔자 백신은 세계보건기구, WHO 권고에 따라 그 해에 유행할 것으로 예상되는 바이러스에 효과가 있도록 만들어지는데, 이번 절기 국가예방접종은 WHO 권고에 맞춘 3가 백신으로 진행됩니다.

감염·보건.content:
어린이 무료 접종 대상 13→14세 확대
21일부터 3가백신 순차적 접종… 코로나19 백신도
▲ 2026-2027절기 인플루엔자 국가예방접종 홍보 포스터. 질병관리청 제공
올 겨울 인플루엔자에 대비해 국가예방접종이 9월 21일부터 어린이와 임신부를 시작으로 순차적으로 진행된다. 올해부턴 접종을 무료로 받을 수 있는 어린이 연령 범위가 기존 13세에서 14세까지 확대됐다.
질병관리청은 내달 21일부터 2027년 4월 30일까지 2026-2027절기 인플루엔자 국가예방접종을 시행한다고 25일 밝혔다. 특히 올해부턴 학령기 청소년의 유행 확산을 막고 집단 보호를 강화하기 위해 기존 생후 6개월~13세까지 지원하던 무료접종 지원 대상을 14세까지로 확대했다. 2012년 1월 1일부터 2026년 8월 31일 출생자까지 무료로 백신을 맞을 수 있다.
접종은 대상별로 순차적으로 이뤄진다. 과거 접종 이력이 없거나 기존 1회만 접종한 생후 6개월 이상 9살 미만 어린이와 임신부는 내달 21일부터 접종할 수 있다. 1회 접종 대상인 생후 6개월~14살 어린이는 28일부터다.
65세 이상 고령층도 연령별로 순차 접종한다. 75세 이상은 10월 12일, 70~74세는 10월 15일, 65~69세는 10월 19일부터 예방접종을 할 수 있다. 또 질병청은 같은 일정으로 고령층 대상 코로나 예방접종도 시작한다며 인플루엔자와 코로나19 백신 동시 접종을 권고했다.
올해 예방접종은 세계보건기구(WHO)가 권장한 바이러스 3종이 모두 포함된 3가 백신이 사용될 예정이다. 접종 대상자는 주소지와 관계없이 가까운 위탁의료기관이나 보건소에서 무료로 할 수 있다. 예방접종 지원 대상이 아닌 경우 유료로 접종할 수 있으며 일부 지자체에서 자체적으로 비용을 지원하고 있어 관할 보건소를 통해 지원 여부를 확인하면 된다.

▲ 인플루엔자 무료접종 확대…9월부터 순차 시행
질병관리청(질병청)은 2026~2027절기 인플루엔자 국가예방접종을 오는 9월 21일부터 2027년 4월 30일까지 시행한다고 25일 밝혔다. 이번 절기부터 어린이 무료 접종 범위가 기존보다 확대돼 생후 6개월부터 14세까지 접종 대상에 포함된다.
접종은 대상별로 순차적으로 진행된다. 9월 21일에는 2회 접종이 필요한 어린이와 임신부를 시작으로, 9월 28일부터는 1회 접종 대상 어린이의 접종이 시작된다. 고령층은 연령에 따라 △75세 이상 10월 12일 △70~74세 10월 15일 △65~69세 10월 19일부터 접종할 수 있다.
무료 접종 대상은 생후 6개월~14세 어린이와 임신부, 65세 이상 어르신이다. 어린이 가운데 과거 인플루엔자 예방접종을 받은 이력이 없거나 1회만 접종한 6개월 이상 9세 미만은 2회 접종 대상이다. 그 외 6개월 이상 14세 이하 어린이는 1회 접종을 받으면 된다.
이번 접종에는 세계보건기구(WHO)가 권고한 바이러스주를 모두 포함한 3가 백신이 사용된다. 주민등록상 주소지와 관계없이 전국 위탁의료기관이나 보건소에서 접종할 수 있으며, 접종기관은 예방접종도우미 누리집에서 확인할 수 있다. 전국 위탁의료기관은 약 2만3000곳이다.
65세 이상 고령층은 인플루엔자와 함께 코로나19 예방접종도 받을 수 있다. 코로나19 백신 역시 10월 12일부터 연령별로 접종이 진행되며, 두 백신은 같은 날 맞는 것도 가능하다. 다만 접종할 때는 각각 다른 부위에 투여해야 한다.
임승관 질병청장은 "인플루엔자 예방접종은 입원과 사망 위험을 낮추고 감염에 따른 사회·경제적 부담을 줄이는 데 중요한 역할을 한다"며 "접종 대상이 14세까지 확대된 만큼 해당 어린이와 보호자의 적극적인 참여를 당부한다"고 말했다.
▲ WHO 평가 1년…감염병 대응 역량도 점검
질병청은 인플루엔자 예방접종과 별도로 국가 차원의 감염병 대응 체계도 점검한다. 세계보건기구(WHO)가 실시한 제2차 합동외부평가(JEE) 1주년을 맞아 권고사항 이행 상황을 확인하고 국제보건규칙(IHR) 관련 세미나를 개최할 예정이다.
JEE는 감염병을 비롯한 각종 공중보건 위협에 대한 국가의 예방·탐지·대응 역량을 국제적인 기준에 따라 평가하는 제도다. 지난해 8월 진행된 2차 평가에는 12개 부처가 참여했으며, 한국은 지속 가능한 공중보건위기 대응 역량을 갖춘 국가로 평가받았다.
당시 평가단은 △국가 IHR 당국 지정 △지속 가능한 재원 조달 체계 마련 △취약계층을 고려한 대응 △지역사회 협력 네트워크 제도화 등 6개 핵심 권고사항을 제시했다.
질병청은 국가 IHR 당국으로서 후속 조치에 대한 이행 상황을 점검한 결과, 6개 핵심 권고를 포함해 전체 19개 영역의 권고사항이 체계적으로 추진되고 있다고 했다.
구체적으로 감염병 위기관리체계 고도화 방안을 마련하고 관련 표준매뉴얼을 개정했으며, 지역사회 소통 네트워크를 제도화하고 범정부 협의기구를 운영하는 등 위기 발생 전 감시와 대응 역량을 강화하고 있다.
25일에는 관계기관 실무자를 대상으로 IHR의 역사와 국가 차원의 이행 필요성을 공유하는 세미나도 열린다. 참석자들은 각 기관의 추진 상황과 현장에서 발생하는 애로사항을 공유하고 향후 협력 방안을 논의할 예정이다.
임승관 청장은 “코로나19 대응 과정에서 얻은 경험을 토대로 국가 감염병 위기관리체계를 지속적으로 보완하고 있다”며 “앞으로도 관계 부처와의 협력을 강화해 공중보건 위기에 대한 국가 대응 역량을 높여 나가겠다”고 말했다.

감염·보건.content:
독감 예방접종 모습
[팍스메디컬뉴스] 올겨울 인플루엔자(독감) 국가예방접종 지원 대상이 14세까지 확대된다. 접종은 9월 21일부터 대상별로 차례로 진행한다.
질병관리청은 다음달 21일부터 내년 4월 30일까지 어린이와 임신부 65세 이상 어르신을 대상으로 2026-2027절기 독감 무료 예방접종을 한다고 25일 밝혔다.
질병관리청에 따르면, 이번 절기 접종부터는 학령기 청소년의 유행 확산을 막기 위해 지원 연령을 기존 생후 6개월에서 13세에서 생후 6개월에서 14세로 확대한다. 지원 대상은 2012년 1월 1일부터 2026년 8월 31일까지 출생한 어린이다.
접종은 대상별로 일정을 나눠 진행한다. 9월 21일부터는 2회 접종 대상 어린이와 임신부를 대상으로 접종한다.
2회 접종 대상 어린이는 과거 접종력이 없거나 1회 접종만 받은 생후 6개월에서 9세 미만 어린이다. 1회 접종 대상인 생후 6개월에서 14세 어린이는 9월 28일부터 접종할 수 있다.
65세 이상 어르신은 10월 12일 75세 이상부터 연령대별로 차례로 접종한다. 코로나19 예방접종도 같은 일정으로 진행돼 두 백신을 함께 맞는 것이 좋다.
이번 국가예방접종에는 세계보건기구(WHO) 권장 바이러스주가 모두 포함된 3가 백신을 사용한다.
대상자는 주소지와 상관없이 전국 2만3000여 개 지정 위탁의료기관이나 보건소에서 무료로 접종받을 수 있다. 지정 의료기관은 예방접종도우미 누리집에서 확인한다.
임승관 질병관리청장은 "독감 예방접종은 입원과 사망 위험을 낮추는 가장 효과적인 수단"이라며 "지원 대상이 14세까지 확대된 만큼 학령기 아동 청소년이 제때 접종받을 수 있도록 학부모의 관심과 참여를 부탁드린다"고 밝혔다.

감염·보건.content:
"여름 독감도 나왔다는데" 올해 독감예방접종 언제부터? 무료대상 및 일정 보니
사진=나남뉴스
최근 폭염으로 냉방기 사용이 늘어나면서 감기와 독감 등 호흡기 감염병에 대한 관심이 높아지고 있다. 특히 어린이와 고령층, 임신부 등 감염에 취약한 계층은 본격적인 겨울철 유행에 앞서 예방접종 일정을 확인할 필요가 있다.
올해는 국가 인플루엔자 예방접종 대상이 확대되면서 지난해와 달라진 부분도 있다. 질병관리청에 따르면 2026~2027절기 인플루엔자 국가예방접종은 오는 9월 21일부터 시작돼 내년 4월 30일까지 이어질 전망이다.
이번 절기 가장 눈에 띄는 변화는 어린이 무료접종 연령이 한 살 늘어난다는 점이다. 기존에는 생후 6개월부터 13세까지였지만 올해부터는 14세까지 국가 지원을 받을 수 있다. 2012년 1월 1일부터 2026년 8월 31일까지 태어난 어린이가 대상이다.
독감, 여름철에도 집단 발생할 수 있어
사진=픽사베이(기사와 관계없는 사진)
접종 시점은 대상에 따라 다르다. 과거 독감 예방접종을 받은 이력이 없거나 접종 횟수가 부족해 2회 접종이 필요한 어린이는 9월 21일부터 무료 접종을 받을 수 있다. 임신부 역시 같은 날부터 접종이 시작된다.
한 차례 접종으로 충분한 생후 6개월~14세 어린이는 9월 28일부터 접종이 가능하다. 어린이와 임신부의 국가예방접종은 내년 4월 30일까지 진행된다. 65세 이상 어르신은 10월부터 순차적으로 접종을 시작한다.
75세 이상은 10월 12일, 70~74세는 10월 15일, 65~69세는 10월 19일부터 접종할 수 있다. 65세 이상을 대상으로 한 코로나19 예방접종도 같은 시기에 진행될 예정이어서 두 백신을 함께 접종하는 것도 권고된다.
사진=질병관리청
무료접종은 주소지와 관계없이 전국 위탁의료기관과 보건소에서 받을 수 있다. 다만 방문하기 전에 해당 기관에서 접종이 가능한지 확인하는 것이 좋다. 예방접종도우미를 통해 가까운 지정 의료기관도 확인할 수 있다.
올해 사용되는 백신은 세계보건기구(WHO)가 권장한 바이러스주가 포함된 3가 백신이다. 독감은 감기와 증상이 비슷하지만 갑작스러운 발열과 오한, 두통, 근육통 등 전신 증상이 나타나는 경우가 많다. 잠복기는 평균 2일로 알려져있다.
따라서 환절기에 목이 아프거나 기침, 발열 등의 증상이 나타났다면 단순 감기로만 판단하기보다 증상을 지켜볼 필요가 있다. 특히 영유아와 고령층, 임신부, 만성질환자 등은 독감으로 인한 합병증 위험이 상대적으로 높아 예방이 중요하다.
아직 본격적인 겨울철 독감 유행이 시작되기 전이지만, 독감은 여름철에도 집단 발생과 산발적인 감염이 가능한 만큼 접종 시기를 놓치지 않도록 미리 일정을 확인하고 접종하는 것이 좋다. 올해는 중학교 2학년 연령대까지 무료 대상에 포함된 만큼 자녀가 지원 대상에 해당하는지 출생일을 기준으로 확인해 보는 것도 필요하다.

감염·보건.content:
# 국·도비 75억원 투입… 생물안전3등급(BL3) 연구시설 본격 운영
# ASF·고병원성 AI·구제역 등 재난형 가축전염병 정밀진단 강화
# 독립 실험공간·원스톱 검사체계 구축… 신속한 초동방역 뒷받침
▲ 전북도 동물위생시험소 '생물안전연구동' 전경
전북특별자치도가 생물안전연구동 구축을 통해 아프리카돼지열병(ASF), 고병원성 조류인플루엔자(HPAI), 구제역 등 재난형 가축전염병에 대한 정밀진단과 방역 대응 역량을 강화한다.
도는 지난 8월 24일 장수군 동물위생시험소에서 ‘생물안전연구동 개소식’을 개최하고 본격적인 운영에 들어간다고 밝혔다.
생물안전연구동은 고위험성 병원체를 안전하게 취급할 수 있는 전문 검사환경을 구축해 재난형 가축전염병을 신속·정확하게 진단하고, 발생 초기 방역 대응을 강화하기 위해 마련됐다.
▲ 지난 24일 전북도는  장수군 동물위생시험소에서 ‘생물안전연구동 개소식’을 개최했다. (사진 / 전북도)
이날 개소식에는 고정삼 전북도 경제부지사를 비롯해 최정록 농림축산검역본부장, 장정복 전북도의회 의원, 정호석 하림 대표이사, 김원일 동물용의약품평가연구원장, 방대섭 전북축산단체연합회장 등 100여 명이 참석했다.
생물안전연구동은 지난 2021년 농림축산식품부 공모사업에 선정돼 국비 30억원과 도비 45억원 등 총사업비 75억원을 투입해 구축했다. 이후 시설 인증·허가기관인 질병관리청의 최종 허가를 받아 운영을 위한 절차를 마쳤다.
생물안전3등급(Biosafety Level 3)은 HPAI, 구제역, ASF 등 고위험성 병원체를 안전하게 취급할 수 있도록 특수 밀폐 및 공조설비 등을 갖춘 전문 실험시설이다.
이번 연구동 개소로 동물위생시험소는 재난형 가축전염병을 보다 안전하고 신속하게 검사할 수 있는 정밀진단 기반을 갖추게 됐다.
특히 독립된 전용 실험공간을 구축해 검사 과정에서 발생할 수 있는 질병 간 교차오염 가능성을 차단하고, 실험자와 주변 환경의 안전성을 높였다.
또한 가축전염병 의심 신고부터 정밀검사까지 신속하게 연계할 수 있는 원스톱 검사체계를 구축해 진단 시간을 단축하고, 검사 결과에 따른 초동방역이 신속하게 이뤄질 수 있도록 대응체계를 강화했다.
도는 앞으로 생물안전연구동을 중심으로 재난형 가축전염병에 대한 상시 진단체계를 운영하고, 진단·연구 전문성을 지속적으로 높여 가축전염병 발생과 확산에 선제적으로 대응할 계획이다.
고정삼 전북도 경제부지사는 “생물안전연구동은 재난형 가축전염병을 신속하고 정확하게 진단하기 위한 전북 동물방역의 핵심 기반시설”이라며 “철저한 진단과 신속한 방역 대응으로 가축전염병 확산을 차단하고 축산농가의 안정적인 경영과 재산 보호에 최선을 다하겠다”고 말했다.

감염·보건.content:
질병관리청은 오는 9월 21일부터 2027년 4월 30일까지 2026~2027절기 인플루엔자 국가예방접종을 실시한다고 26일 밝혔다(사진 출처: 게티이미지).
올겨울부터 인플루엔자 국가예방접종 지원 대상이 기존 13세에서 14세까지로 확대된다. 접종은 오는 9월 21일부터 대상별로 순차적으로 시작한다.
질병관리청은 오는 9월 21일부터 2027년 4월 30일까지 2026~2027절기 인플루엔자 국가예방접종을 실시한다고 26일 밝혔다.
이번 절기부터 어린이 무료접종 대상은 기존 생후 6개월~13세에서 생후 6개월~14세로 확대된다. 이에 따라 2012년 1월 1일부터 2026년 8월 31일까지 출생한 어린이가 무료로 접종받을 수 있다.
질병청은 학령기 청소년의 인플루엔자 유행 확산을 막고 집단 보호를 강화하기 위해 지원 대상을 확대했다고 설명했다.
접종 시작일은 대상별로 다르다. 과거 인플루엔자 예방접종을 받은 적이 없거나 기존에 1회만 접종한 생후 6개월 이상 9세 미만 어린이 등 2회 접종 대상자는 9월 21일부터 접종할 수 있다. 임신부 접종도 같은 날 시작한다.
2회 접종 대상자를 제외한 생후 6개월 이상 14세 어린이는 9월 28일부터 접종할 수 있다. 2회 접종 대상 어린이가 인플루엔자 유행 전에 접종을 마칠 수 있도록 1회 접종 대상자보다 일주일 먼저 시작한다.
65세 이상은 10월부터 연령별로 순차적으로 접종을 시작한다. 75세 이상은 10월 12일, 70~74세는 10월 15일, 65~69세는 10월 19일부터 접종할 수 있다. 접종 초기 대상자가 한꺼번에 몰리는 것을 막고 안전사고를 예방하기 위해 연령별로 시작일을 달리했다.
65세 이상 코로나19 예방접종도 10월 12일부터 같은 일정으로 진행된다. 질병청은 인플루엔자와 코로나19 백신의 동시 접종을 권고한다. 두 백신을 동시에 맞을 경우 각각 다른 부위에 접종해야 한다.
이번 절기 인플루엔자 국가예방접종에는 세계보건기구(WHO) 권장주가 포함된 3가 백신이 사용된다.
대상자는 주소지와 관계없이 가까운 위탁의료기관이나 보건소에서 무료로 접종할 수 있다. 전국 위탁의료기관은 약 2만3,000곳으로, 관할 보건소나 예방접종도우미 홈페이지에서 확인할 수 있다.
국가예방접종 지원 대상이 아니면 인플루엔자 예방접종을 시행하는 의료기관에서 비용을 내고 접종할 수 있다. 일부 지방자치단체는 자체적으로 접종 비용을 지원하고 있어 관할 보건소에서 지원 여부를 확인하면 된다.
임승관 질병청장은 “인플루엔자 예방접종은 어린이, 임신부, 노인 모두에게 인플루엔자로 인한 입원과 사망을 줄이고 질병 부담을 낮추는 데 매우 효과적인 수단”이라며 “이번 절기부터 국가예방접종 지원 대상이 14세까지 확대된 만큼 해당 학령기 아동·청소년이 일정에 맞춰 접종받을 수 있도록 학부모들의 관심과 참여를 당부드린다”고 말했다.

감염·보건.content:
올겨울 인플루엔자 국가예방접종 지원 대상이 14세까지 확대되고 접종은 9월 21일부터 순차적으로 시작된다.
질병관리청은 9월 21일부터 내년 4월 30일까지 어린이와 임신부, 65세 이상 어르신을 대상으로 2026~2027절기 인플루엔자 무료 예방접종을 실시한다고 밝혔다.
특히 이번 절기부터 학령기 청소년의 인플루엔자 유행 확산을 막기 위해 어린이 지원 연령을 기존 생후 6개월~13세에서 생후 6개월~14세로 확대한다.
2012년 1월 1일부터 2026년 8월 31일까지 출생한 어린이가 대상이다.
접종은 대상별 일정에 따라 순차적으로 진행된다.
9월 21일부터 인플루엔자 백신을 2회 맞아야 하는 어린이와 임신부를 대상으로 접종을 시작한다.
2회 접종 대상은 과거 접종력이 없거나 기존에 백신을 한 차례만 접종한 생후 6개월 이상 9세 미만 어린이다.
2회 접종 대상이 아닌 생후 6개월 이상 14세 어린이의 1회 접종은 9월 28일부터 시작한다.
65세 이상 어르신은 10월 12일 75세 이상을 시작으로 연령대별로 순차적으로 접종받을 수 있다.
이번 국가예방접종에는 세계보건기구가 권장한 바이러스주가 모두 포함된 3가 인플루엔자 백신이 사용된다.
접종 대상자는 주소지와 관계없이 가까운 위탁의료기관이나 보건소에서 무료로 접종받을 수 있다.
전국 약 2만 3000개 위탁의료기관은 관할 보건소에 문의하거나 예방접종도우미 누리집에서 확인할 수 있다.
누리집에서는 '예방접종관리'의 '지정의료기관 찾기' 메뉴를 이용하면 된다.
한편, 65세 이상을 대상으로 하는 코로나19 예방접종도 같은 일정으로 시행되며, 인플루엔자 백신과 코로나19 백신의 동시 접종이 권고된다.
전국에 인플루엔자(독감) 환자가 증가하는 가운데 26일 오후 서울 시내 한 의원에 독감과 코로나19 백신 접종 안내 포스터가 붙어 있다. 방역당국은 지난 20일자로 전국에 독감 유행주의보를 발령한 바 있다. 2024.12.26 (사진=저작권자(c) 연합뉴스, 무단 전재-재배포 금지)
임승관 질병관리청장은 "인플루엔자 예방접종은 어린이와 임신부, 어르신의 인플루엔자로 인한 입원과 사망을 줄이고 질병 부담을 낮추는 데 매우 효과적인 수단"이라며 "이번 절기부터 국가예방접종 지원 대상이 14세까지 확대된 만큼 해당 학령기 아동·청소년이 일정에 맞춰 접종받을 수 있도록 학부모들의 관심과 참여를 당부드린다"고 밝혔다.
문의: 질병관리청 예방접종관리과(043-719-8365)

감염·보건.content:
∎ 어린이 독감 국가예방접종 대상 14세(중학교 2학년)까지 확대
∎ 9월 21일부터 2회 접종 대상 어린이 및 임신부, 9월 28일부터 1회 접종 대상 어린이 접종 시작
∎ 10월 12일부터 75세 이상을 시작으로 65세 이상 연령대별 순차적 접종 시작
그림출처 Pixabay, Alexandra_Koch
[탐사일보 김리든 기자] 질병관리청(청장 임승관)은 오는 9월 21일부터 2027년 4월 30일까지 2026-2027절기 독감(인플루엔자) 국가예방접종을 시작할 계획이다.
다가오는 겨울 독감 유행에 대비하여 어린이, 임신부, 어르신 대상 무료 예방접종을 실시하며, 특히 이번 절기부터는 학령기 청소년의 유행 확산을 방지하고 집단 보호를 강화하기 위하여 기존 '생후 6개월~13세'까지 지원하던 어린이 대상 연령을 '생후 6개월~14세(2012.1.1.~2026.8.31.출생자)'까지 확대하여 시행한다.
9월 21일(월)에 2회 접종 대상 어린이* 및 임신부를 시작으로, 9월 28일(월)은 1회 접종 대상 어린이**, 10월 12일(월)에는 75세 이상 어르신부터 연령대별 순차적으로 독감 국가예방접종이 시행된다.
* (2회 접종 대상) 과거 접종력이 없거나, 기존에 1회만 접종받은 6개월 이상 9세 미만 어린이
** (1회 접종 대상) 2회 접종 대상 외 6개월 이상 14세 어린이
자료제공 질병관리청
2026-2027절기 독감 국가예방접종은 세계보건기구(WHO) 권장주가 모두 포함된 3가 백신으로 접종이 진행되며, 주소지와 관계없이 가까운 위탁의료기관 및 보건소에서 접종 가능하다.
전국 위탁의료기관은 약 2.3만 개소로 관할 보건소 또는 예방접종도우미 누리집*에서 가까운 위탁의료기관을 확인할 수 있다.
* 예방접종도우미 누리집(nip.kdca.go.kr) > 예방접종관리 > 지정의료기관 찾기
질병관리청 임승관 청장은 "독감 예방접종은 어린이, 임신부, 어르신 모두에게 독감으로 인한 입원과 사망을 줄이고 질병 부담을 낮추는데 매우 효과적인 수단"이라며, "이번 절기부터 독감 국가예방접종 지원 대상이 14세까지 확대된 만큼, 해당 학령기 아동·청소년이 일정에 맞춰 접종받을 수 있도록 학부모들의 관심과 참여를 당부드린다"라고 전했다.

감염·보건.content:
관내 위탁의료기관 15곳에서 HVP 4가 백신 무료로 접종 가능
[ 타임즈 - 김시창 기자 ] 인천시 영종구는 ‘12세 남성 청소년 HPV 예방접종 사업’에 대한 구민들의 적극적인 관심과 참여를 26일 당부했다.
이는 기존 12~17세 여성 청소년과 18~26세 저소득층 여성 등을 중심으로 지원이 이뤄지던 ‘HPV 국가 예방접종 사업’의 대상 범위가 올해 5월부터 12세 남성 청소년까지 확대된 데 따른 것이다.
‘HPV(인유두종바이러스)’는 자궁경부암의 주요 원인 중 하나로 남녀 모두에게 감염될 수 있으며, 남성에게도 구인두암, 항문암, 생식기 사마귀 등 다양한 질환을 유발하는 것으로 알려져 있다.
이에 세계보건기구(WHO)와 여러 국가에서는 남녀 모두를 대상으로 HPV 백신 접종을 권고하고 있으며, 적기에 접종해야 백신의 최대 효과를 기대할 수 있어 권장 횟수에 맞춰 끝까지 접종을 완료하는 것이 좋다.
접종 대상인 12세 남성 청소년(올해 기준 2014년 출생자)은 관내 HPV 국가 예방접종 위탁의료기관 15곳을 방문하면 무료로 HPV 4가 백신을 접종받을 수 있다.
해당자는 6개월 간격으로 2회 접종하면 된다.
구는 해당 청소년들의 백신 접종을 적극 독려하기 위해 관내 초등학교에 예방접종 안내 공문을 발송함은 물론, 문자 메시지, 사회관계망서비스(SNS) 등 다양한 채널을 통해 홍보활동을 전개하고 있다.
영종구 관계자는 “HPV 예방접종은 더 이상 여성들만의 문제가 아니라 모든 아이에게 필요한 조치”라며 “우리 아이들의 건강한 미래를 위해 이번 예방접종에 대한 더욱 적극적인 관심과 참여를 바란다”라고 밝혔다.
더 자세한 사항은 영종구보건소 예방접종실로 문의하거나 질병관리청 예방접종도우미를 참고하면 된다.

감염·보건.content:
김제시청
[엔디엔뉴스 황장하 기자] 김제시는 가을철 야외활동이 증가하는 시기를 앞두고 감염병 예방을 위해 어르신 폐렴구균 및 신증후군출혈열 예방접종에 적극 참여해 줄 것을 당부했다.
어르신 폐렴구균 예방접종은 폐렴구균 감염에 따른 중증 감염과 합병증을 예방하기 위한 국가예방 접종사업으로, 65세 이상(1961.12.31.이전 출생자) 어르신 중 폐렴구균 23가 다당 백신을 접종하지 않은 대상자는 연중 무료로 1회 접종할 수 있다. 위탁의료기관(주소지와 관계 없음) 또는 보건소·보건진료소에서 접종 가능하며, 접종 전 본인의 과거 접종력을 확인하는 것이 중요하다.
이와 함께 신증후군출혈열 예방접종도 농업인 등 고위험군을 중심으로 적극 권고된다. 신증후군출혈열은 들쥐 등 설치류의 배설물과 접촉하는 과정에서 감염될 수 있어 농작업이나 야외활동이 잦은 경우 각별한 주의가 필요하다.
신증후군출혈열 예방접종은 1개월 간격으로 2회 접종한 후 12개월 뒤 3차 접종하는 방식으로 진행되므로, 접종 대상자는 접종 일정을 미리 확인하고 예방접종에 참여하는 것이 중요하다. 예방접종은 보건소 및 관내 보건진료소에서 무료로 접종 받을 수 있으며, 접종 대상 여부와 접종 일정 등 자세한 사항은 방문 전 확인하는 것이 좋다.
정성주 김제시장은“어르신과 농업인 등 예방접종이 필요한 시민들이 적기에 접종해 건강하고 안전한 일상을 이어갈 수 있도록 적극적인 관심과 참여를 당부드린다”고 말했다.

Drugs & Therapies.url_match_title: SillaJen wins US FDA orphan status for AML drug BAL0891 - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
Drugs & Therapies.content: SillaJen(215600) said on the 25th that its anticancer candidate “BAL0891” has been designated an orphan drug for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). BAL0891 is a first-in-class anticancer candidate that simultaneously targets TTK and PLK1, key proteins involved in cancer cell division. It is currently in a global phase 1 trial for solid tumors and blood cancers. The FDA’s orphan drug designation is granted to medicines being developed for rare diseases that affect fewer than 200,000 patients in the United States. SillaJen, with this designation, can receive benefits including ▲ eligibility to apply for FDA clinical research funding programs ▲ a 25% tax credit on clinical trial expense in the United States ▲ FDA advice and expedited review support for clinical trial plans ▲ a waiver of new drug application fees. If final marketing approval is obtained, the company can also secure, in principle, seven years of market exclusivity in the United States for the same drug and indication. AML, the target of this designation, is a blood cancer in which white blood cells in the bone marrow turn into cancer cells and proliferate rapidly. Early symptoms are not distinct, making early diagnosis difficult, and the disease tends to worsen quickly. Traditionally, highly toxic anticancer drugs or bone marrow transplants have been used, but side effects and the risk of relapse have been cited as limitations. Targeted therapies have emerged in recent years, but drug resistance can develop during treatment. SillaJen expects that, because BAL0891 simultaneously targets key factors involved in cancer cell division, it could offer a new treatment option for AML patients who have developed resistance to existing therapies. A SillaJen official said, “Because it was designated as an orphan drug from the early clinical stage, we see this as a degree of recognition of BAL0891’s medical importance and potential,” adding, “based on this achievement, we will do our best to deliver more positive results in the remaining clinical schedule.”

Drugs & Therapies.content:
Eppe launch, $2.3 bil. licensing deal for HM17321 fuel investor optimism
Hanmi Pharmaceutical headquarters in Songpa District, Seoul / Courtesy of Hanmi Pharmaceutical
Hanmi Pharmaceutical is gaining attention as it prepares to launch Korea’s first glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-based obesity drug, Eppe, while also signing a licensing deal worth up to $2.3 billion for a separate obesity drug candidate.
In recent weeks, a series of analysts at domestic brokerages have raised their price target on Hanmi Pharm, citing the company’s potential in obesity drugs.
“We expect Hanmi Pharm’s corporate value to increase with the upcoming domestic approval and launch of efpeglenatide (Eppe), as well as the release of Phase 1 trial results for HM17321,” DS Securities analyst Kim Min-jeong said in a report on Tuesday, raising the company’s price target to 720,000 won ($519) from 680,000 won.
Samsung Securities on Tuesday also raised its price target on Hanmi Pharm to 610,000 won, up from 500,000 won, citing the potential of HM17321.
Eppe and HM17321 are key drugs and drug candidates in Hanmi Pharm’s obesity treatment pipeline. Eppe is a long-acting GLP-1 obesity treatment based on Lapscovery, Hanmi Pharm’s own platform technology.
The drug was initially licensed out to global pharmaceutical company Sanofi in 2015 as a diabetes treatment, but the rights were returned in 2020. Hanmi Pharm then decided to develop the drug as its own obesity treatment.
The company applied for approval from Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety in December 2025, and the application is currently under review, with Hanmi Pharm saying it will be able to launch the drug in the second half of this year.
If launched, Eppe will become the first GLP-1-based obesity treatment developed by a Korean pharmaceutical company. It also can be Korea’s 44th domestically developed novel drug.
Eppe is also expected to be priced more aggressively than leading GLP-1-based obesity treatments such as Wegovy and Mounjaro. Because Hanmi Pharm plans to manufacture the drug at its own biopharmaceutical plant in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province, it is also expected to provide a more stable supply in the Korean market.
“Eppe is more than just a new drug. It represents the legacy of Hanmi Pharm’s decades-long commitment to innovative drug development,” a Hanmi Pharm official said.
“We plan to develop Eppe beyond an obesity treatment into a key therapeutic option for a broader range of metabolic diseases.”
A screen capture from Hanmi Pharmaceutical's documentary on its obesity treatment pipeline / Courtesy of Hanmi Pharmaceutical
HM17321 is a drug candidate that aims to become a first-in-class treatment capable of reducing fat while preserving muscle mass, overcoming a key limitation of existing GLP-1-based obesity treatments. It received a U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval on its Phase 1 investigational new drug application in November 2025, and the trial is currently underway.
On Monday, Hanmi Pharm signed a deal to license out the candidate to Genentech, a subsidiary of global pharmaceutical giant Roche.
Under the deal, Hanmi Pharm will receive an upfront payment of $190 million and could receive up to $2.3 billion including milestone payments. The upfront payment is the largest ever received by a Korean pharmaceutical company for a single drug candidate.
Genentech will be responsible for the development, manufacturing and commercialization of HM17321 worldwide except Korea, while Hanmi Pharm will retain the domestic rights. Hanmi Pharm plans to complete the ongoing Phase 1 trial, and Genentech will take over development from Phase 2. Hanmi Pharm will also receive separate royalties after commercialization.
“According to the company’s announcement at American Diabetes Association in June, HM17321 has shown efficacy in not only obesity and diabetes but also in in a model of age-related muscle loss,” Hana Securities analyst Kim Seon-a said.
“Despite being an early-stage pipeline candidate, the deal is worth up to $2.3 billion, because of its high potential for combination therapies and its potential to expand beyond diabetes and obesity into sarcopenia.”

How big is Novel Hypercholesterolemia Drugs Market in 2026?
USD 17.6 billion in 2026 and USD 42.8 billion by 2036 at a 9.3% CAGR.
Demand for novel hypercholesterolemia drugs is projected to expand at
9.3% CAGR
between 2026 and 2036, increasing valuation from
USD 17.6 billion
in 2026 to
USD 42.8 billion
by 2036. Commercial growth is moving across injectable antibodies, long-acting RNA therapies, oral nonstatin drugs and clinical-stage gene-editing programs that address patients who remain above LDL-C goals.
Treatment choice is widening as guidance and regulatory decisions recognize more routes to LDL-C reduction. The 2026 ACC/AHA Guideline on the Management of Dyslipidemia sets risk-based LDL-C goals, while the July 2026 FDA approval of Lipfendra adds the first once-daily oral PCSK9 inhibitor. These changes increase the value of evidence that links efficacy, route and access requirements to a defined patient group.
Novel Hypercholesterolemia Drugs Market Value Analysis
Key Takeaways of Novel Hypercholesterolemia Drugs Market
LDL-C lowering is moving across injectable, oral and gene-silencing routes as prescribers seek additional options for patients who remain above risk-based goals.
PCSK9 inhibitors are projected at 42.0% share in 2026 because marketed antibodies, inclisiran and oral enlicitide connect one validated pathway with several dosing models.
Primary hypercholesterolemia is estimated at 46.0% of indication demand in 2026 due to the broad treatment need across non-familial disease and heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia.
Injectable therapies are forecast at 57.0% by route of administration in 2026, supported by established antibody and siRNA products administered subcutaneously or by infusion.
Clinical outcome evidence, safety monitoring and reimbursement criteria limit adoption when a new modality adds cost or specialist administration without a clear care pathway.
Amgen Inc., Novartis AG, Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Esperion Therapeutics, Inc., Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Merck & Co., Inc., Eli Lilly and Company, Verve Therapeutics, Inc., CRISPR Therapeutics AG and Silence Therapeutics plc are active across marketed and clinical-stage lipid-lowering routes.
Analyst Perspective
"Novel hypercholesterolemia drugs are creating a choice between dosing frequency, route and durability. Commercial adoption will depend on whether each therapy reaches the intended LDL-C goal with evidence that payers and care teams can use in routine practice."
-
Anurag Sharma
, Principal Consultant, Future Market Insights
How is the Novel Hypercholesterolemia Drugs Market segmented?
The novel hypercholesterolemia drugs market is segmented by drug class, indication, route of administration, end user, distribution channel and region.
Drug class separates PCSK9 inhibition, siRNA, ATP citrate lyase inhibition, ANGPTL3 targeting and gene editing. Indication covers primary and familial hypercholesterolemia, mixed dyslipidemia and
cardiovascular risk reduction
. Route of administration distinguishes injectable and oral formats. End user and distribution channel show where prescribing, administration and dispensing occur across hospitals, clinics and pharmacy networks.
Why do PCSK9 Inhibitors lead the Drug Class category?
Novel Hypercholesterolemia Drugs Market Analysis By Drug Class
PCSK9 inhibition increases LDL-receptor recycling and supports several delivery models. Repatha prescribing information describes a subcutaneous monoclonal antibody, while Leqvio prescribing information identifies inclisiran as an siRNA directed to PCSK9 mRNA. Lipfendra extends the same pathway to a daily oral tablet.
Based on drug class,
PCSK9 inhibitors
are projected to account for 42.0% in 2026 because the pathway is represented by marketed antibody, siRNA and oral therapies.
Monoclonal antibodies provide established LDL-C reduction, while inclisiran supports twice-yearly maintenance dosing after the initial and three-month injections. Oral enlicitide reduces the administration barrier for patients who prefer a tablet, although adherence and reimbursement remain important.
Why does Primary Hypercholesterolemia lead the Indication category?
Primary hypercholesterolemia includes non-familial disease and heterozygous
familial hypercholesterolemia
across a broad adult population. The European Medicines Agency overview for Leqvio covers adults with primary hypercholesterolaemia or mixed dyslipidaemia, showing how one therapy can serve several common lipid-management pathways.
In 2026, primary hypercholesterolemia is expected to lead the indication category with 46.0% share because it covers a wider treatment population than rare homozygous disease.
Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia requires earlier and sustained LDL-C control, while non-familial disease creates larger treatment volumes across cardiology, internal medicine and primary care. Mixed dyslipidemia and secondary prevention add adjacent demand.
Why do Injectable therapies lead the Route of Administration category?
The leading marketed modalities entered practice as subcutaneous or intravenous therapies. Repatha is administered subcutaneously, Leqvio uses healthcare-professional subcutaneous dosing and Evkeeza prescribing information specifies a monthly intravenous infusion for homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia.
The injectable category is likely to capture 57.0% share in 2026 due to established antibody and siRNA products with defined administration schedules.
Long-acting injections can reduce dosing frequency but require appointment capacity and follow-up. Oral bempedoic acid and enlicitide widen at-home treatment, while gene-editing programs remain dependent on clinical evidence and specialized delivery.
Why do Hospitals lead the End User category?
Hospitals bring lipid specialists, cardiology services and infusion capacity into one setting for patients with severe LDL-C elevation or complex cardiovascular risk. This matters for intravenous treatment, treatment initiation and the monitoring required when therapy is added to an existing regimen.
Hospitals are projected to lead the end user category with 38.0% share in 2026 because they coordinate specialist assessment, administration and follow-up for high-risk patients.
Cardiology departments and lipid clinics manage treatment escalation, while internal medicine departments support patients with diabetes, hypertension or other risk factors. Ambulatory centers and specialty clinics extend administration outside large hospitals.
Why do Hospital Pharmacies lead the Distribution Channel category?
Hospital pharmacies support prescription review, cold-chain handling and provider-administered therapy within the same care pathway. They are positioned to coordinate high-cost injectables and infusion products where payer authorization or specialist confirmation is required before treatment.
Hospital pharmacies are forecast to lead the distribution channel category with 41.0% share in 2026 owing to their role in specialist prescribing and controlled administration.
Retail and specialty pharmacies are more relevant for oral therapies and self-administered injections. Specialty distribution remains important for biologics, while online channels depend on national dispensing rules and the route of administration.
What are the drivers, restraints and opportunities in the Novel Hypercholesterolemia Drugs Market?
Risk-based LDL-C goals support treatment escalation while evidence, reimbursement and administration requirements determine whether new modalities enter routine care.
Driver:
Updated lipid guidance and broader regulatory labels expand the population considered for additional nonstatin LDL-C lowering.
Restraint:
High treatment cost, specialist administration and incomplete long-term outcome evidence can slow payer approval or physician adoption.
Opportunity:
Oral PCSK9 inhibition, hepatic
RNA interference
and one-time gene editing can create new treatment paths if clinical benefit and access are established.
The main demand driver is the gap between measured LDL-C and the goal set for a patient's cardiovascular risk. The 2026 ACC/AHA dyslipidemia guideline restores explicit LDL-C and non-HDL-C goals and supports earlier treatment discussion for people at elevated risk. Broader labels for Repatha and Leqvio also allow use before a cardiovascular event in selected patients.
The main restraint is implementation. Injectable and infusion therapies require reliable administration, while high-cost drugs can involve prior authorization or step-therapy rules. New genetic medicines add uncertainty around durability, off-target effects and long-term follow-up, which can keep adoption within specialist centers during early commercialization.
The main opportunity is a wider modality mix. Lipfendra introduces oral PCSK9 inhibition, zodasiran advances ANGPTL3 RNA interference in Phase 3 for homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia and CTX310 tests one-time in vivo
gene editing
. Each route can address a different barrier involving frequency, adherence or biological target.

How do country-level CAGRs compare in the Novel Hypercholesterolemia Drugs Market?
The seven country CAGRs span 1.5 percentage points, from South Korea at 10.1% to Japan at 8.6%. The range is narrow enough that access conditions, treatment guidelines and reimbursement design can matter more than the headline difference between two neighboring rates.
South Korea records the highest CAGR at 10.1%, supported by specialist lipid care and clinical interest in PCSK9, siRNA and gene-targeted approaches.
The USA is forecast at 9.7%, 0.4 percentage points below South Korea, with growth supported by updated dyslipidemia guidance and the first oral PCSK9 approval.
Canada is projected at 9.4%, 0.3 percentage points below the USA, as national authorization and provincial access decisions shape uptake.
The UK is estimated at 9.2%, 0.2 percentage points below Canada, with NICE criteria linking inclisiran use to defined cardiovascular and LDL-C thresholds.
Germany is forecast at 9.0%, 0.2 percentage points below the UK, as benefit assessment keeps comparative evidence central to reimbursement.
Australia also records 9.0%, matching Germany, with PBS listings supporting access to evolocumab and inclisiran under authority restrictions.
Japan is projected at 8.6%, 0.4 percentage points below Germany and Australia, while the 2025 approval of bempedoic acid adds an oral nonstatin option.
Similar growth rates can produce different commercial entry conditions. The full report evaluates regulatory status, reimbursement, prescribing pathways and product availability across North America, Western Europe, East Asia, South Asia and Pacific, Latin America, Eastern Europe, and the Middle East and Africa.
Country-wise Analysis
South Korea combines specialist cardiovascular care with an active national clinical community focused on dyslipidemia. The Korean Guidelines for the Management of Dyslipidemia, 5th edition include PCSK9 inhibitors for selected patients who remain above LDL-C targets, while the Dyslipidemia Fact Sheet 2024 continues national tracking of diagnosis and control. South Korea is forecast to expand at 10.1% CAGR through 2036 as treatment escalation and interest in long-acting or gene-targeted modalities broaden the addressable specialist population.
The USA has the broadest recent change in treatment choice. The 2026 ACC/AHA guideline sets explicit LDL-C goals across risk groups, and the FDA approval of Lipfendra in July 2026 adds a once-daily oral PCSK9 inhibitor for adults with hypercholesterolemia, including heterozygous familial disease. The USA is estimated to grow at 9.7% CAGR as earlier risk-based treatment and more route options expand prescribing beyond established injectable pathways.
Canada has national regulatory access to PCSK9 antibodies and inclisiran, while public reimbursement remains organized through federal, provincial and territorial processes. Health Canada's 2021 product highlights identify Leqvio for additional LDL-C reduction in adults with heterozygous familial or non-familial hypercholesterolemia under specified treatment conditions. Canada is projected to advance at 9.4% CAGR through 2036, although plan-level criteria and price review will continue to influence the pace of adoption.
The UK links new lipid-lowering treatment to explicit health-technology assessment criteria. NICE technology appraisal TA733 recommends inclisiran as an option for adults with primary hypercholesterolaemia or mixed dyslipidaemia when the defined cardiovascular and LDL-C conditions are met. The UK is forecast to record 9.2% CAGR as structured NHS access supports eligible patients, while treatment thresholds limit use outside the recommended population.
Germany provides access within a reimbursement system that gives strong weight to comparative benefit. The Federal Joint Committee assessment of inclisiran concluded that additional benefit was not proven for the assessed groups because suitable comparative data were not presented. Germany is expected to grow at 9.0% CAGR, with demand supported by cardiovascular prevention but constrained by the need to demonstrate value against established alternatives.
Australia combines specialist prescribing with national subsidy rules. The PBS listing for inclisiran covers heterozygous familial and non-familial hypercholesterolaemia under streamlined authority, while evolocumab remains listed for familial and non-familial indications under defined restrictions. Australia is forecast at 9.0% CAGR as subsidized access supports eligible patients, although authority requirements keep treatment focused on higher-risk groups.
Japan has an established specialist market for familial hypercholesterolemia and continues to add nonstatin options. The PMDA list of approved drugs records the September 2025 approval of Nexletol, containing bempedoic acid, for hypercholesterolemia and familial hypercholesterolemia. Japan is projected to expand at 8.6% CAGR through 2036 as oral therapy broadens choice, while local evidence and reimbursement decisions shape uptake across older and high-risk patients.

Amgen Inc., Novartis AG, Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Esperion Therapeutics, Inc., Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Merck & Co., Inc., Eli Lilly and Company, Verve Therapeutics, Inc., CRISPR Therapeutics AG and Silence Therapeutics plc are the notable companies serving the novel hypercholesterolemia drugs market.
Novel Hypercholesterolemia Drugs Market Analysis By Company
Competition extends from marketed LDL-C therapies to late-stage RNA interference and early gene-editing programs. Commercial suppliers compete on LDL-C reduction, cardiovascular evidence, dosing frequency and payer access. Clinical-stage companies compete on durability, target selection and the safety evidence needed to move genetic medicines into broader cardiovascular care.
Amgen, Novartis, Regeneron, Esperion and Merck supply marketed products across PCSK9 inhibition, ANGPTL3 inhibition and ATP citrate lyase inhibition.
Arrowhead and Silence Therapeutics develop RNA interference programs for inherited or residual lipid risk.

Drugs & Therapies.url_match_title: Bristol-Myers Squibb stock holds above $67 as new myeloma drug gains FDA approval - Ad-hoc-news.de
Drugs & Therapies.content:
Bristol-Myers Squibb US1078421011 geometrisches Bauhaus-Poster mit dem Sektor-Text PHARMA in kräftigen Primärfarben, Illustration mit AI erstellt.
Bristol-Myers Squibb Inc. (ISIN US1078421011) stock traded at $67.28 at the New York Stock Exchange close on August 24, 2026, with a flat after-hours indication that kept the shares in the high-$60 range as investors digest fresh FY 2026 earnings guidance and a newly approved multiple myeloma therapy.
Shares consolidate around fresh 52-week highs
Per a real-time quote overview, Bristol-Myers Squibb shares finished regular US trading at $67.28 on August 24, 2026, up $0.27 or 0.40 percent on the day, with the same level quoted in post-market dealings later that afternoon.
The BMY quote snapshot
also highlights a 52-week trading band with a low of $40.00 and a recent high near $80.00, placing the current price much closer to the upper end of the range than to the floor.
Several institutional-investor filings published on August 25, 2026, show investors increasing exposure at these levels. One Form 13F-based summary reports that a large asset manager purchased 17,022,940 Bristol-Myers Squibb shares in the second quarter of 2026, valuing the stake at $980,862,000 and equating to ownership of 0.83 percent of the company’s equity as of the filing date.
The institutional-activity overview
notes that hedge funds and other institutional investors collectively hold 76.41 percent of Bristol-Myers Squibb stock outstanding, underscoring deep professional participation.
Consensus data compiled in these same filings point to a constructive sell-side view. Across a broad analyst set, Bristol-Myers Squibb currently carries an average rating characterized as Moderate Buy, with one Strong Buy, thirteen Buy, ten Hold and one Sell recommendation reflected in the tally. The consensus 12-month price objective cited in the data stands at $66.06, marginally below the late-August trading price but still broadly aligned with the current level.
An analyst-consensus summary
shows the same $66.06 target alongside the rating mix, giving investors a benchmark against which to frame valuation.
FY 2026 earnings guidance and valuation backdrop
A recent fundamentals overview linked to new institutional positions indicates that Bristol-Myers Squibb has published FY 2026 guidance of $6.75 to $7.00 in earnings per share, providing a clearer profitability roadmap for the current year.
The FY 2026 guidance note
presents this EPS range explicitly as management’s outlook.
Using the late-August 2026 share price of $67.28 and the mid-point of the EPS guidance range of $6.875, Bristol-Myers Squibb trades on a forward price-to-earnings multiple close to 9.8 times FY 2026 earnings. That multiple compares to higher valuation levels seen historically for large-cap biopharmaceutical names, reflecting that the company’s stock is priced at less than ten times the guided current-year earnings despite recent gains toward the upper half of its 52-week range.
This valuation context matters for investors assessing the balance between growth prospects and risk. On the one hand, the consensus target of $66.06 is only slightly below the latest trading price, suggesting limited upside embedded in near-term analyst models. On the other, a forward price-to-earnings ratio under 10 leaves room for multiple expansion if new products scale faster than expected or if margins improve relative to guidance. The interplay between a moderate rating, concentrated institutional ownership and a relatively modest earnings multiple helps explain why Bristol-Myers Squibb stock has held steady in the high-$60s rather than correcting sharply after its recent run.
FDA approval of CELMoD iberdomide strengthens oncology pipeline
Beyond earnings guidance and positioning, a meaningful catalyst for Bristol-Myers Squibb in August 2026 comes from US regulatory action on a novel multiple myeloma therapy. A detailed scientific report explains that following strong early clinical results, the US Food and Drug Administration has granted accelerated approval to iberdomide, branded by Bristol-Myers Squibb as Zenbexus, as the first example of what the company terms the CELMoD class of molecular glue protein degraders.
The protein-degrader approval article
describes iberdomide as a therapy that promotes targeted degradation of specific proteins to combat cancer cells.
In terms of treatment regimen, the FDA decision covers iberdomide in a combination including the anti-cancer monoclonal antibody daratumumab for multiple myeloma patients whose disease has relapsed and no longer responds to prior therapies. The coverage emphasizes that iberdomide, in this setting, is the first multiple myeloma drug cleared for use based on minimal residual disease metrics, indicating efficacy even when disease burden has been reduced to very low levels. This minimal residual disease data was central to the accelerated approval and sets a precedent for future regulatory evaluations of similar agents.
A separate pharmacy-focused overview lists Zenbexus (iberdomide) among six new FDA-approved drugs, noting that the FDA decision for Zenbexus was dated August 13, 2026.
The pharmacy update
specifies that Zenbexus is approved for use alongside daratumumab, hyaluronidase-fihj and dexamethasone in adults with multiple myeloma who have received at least one prior line of therapy, including both a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory agent. This positioning places the CELMoD therapy in the relapsed setting, where treatment options can be limited and new mechanisms of action are particularly valuable.
For Bristol-Myers Squibb, this approval adds another advanced oncology asset to its portfolio and reinforces its strategy of developing innovative immune-oncology and hematology drugs. While precise revenue projections for iberdomide are not yet detailed in the cited materials, the fact that the drug is first-in-class in the CELMoD category and supported by minimal residual disease-based evidence suggests meaningful potential in a segment of the multiple myeloma market that often faces unmet needs. The regulatory milestone, coming within weeks of the company’s FY 2026 EPS guidance communication, supports the narrative that pipeline execution remains central to Bristol-Myers Squibb’s medium-term growth story.
Analyst upgrades and technical backdrop
The valuation and pipeline context is complemented by recent changes in individual analyst views referenced in market data. A quote summary for Bristol-Myers Squibb highlights an August 5, 2026 rating action, noting that one research house raised its recommendation on the stock to Buy and set a price target of $75.00. The same data table pairs this call with the broader consensus, which still centers on a Moderate Buy stance with the $66.06 target already mentioned.
The analyst action table
lists the August 5, 2026 upgrade and the associated $75.00 objective, giving context for the upper bound of expectations.
On the technical side, several institutional-position reports echo the same price level for Bristol-Myers Squibb on August 25, 2026, noting that shares of NYSE:BMY or BMY stock opened at $67.30 on that date.
One such technical overview
states that the company’s 50-day moving average stands at $60.77 and its 200-day moving average at $59.47, indicating that the current trading price is clearly above both intermediate and longer-term trend lines.
The gap between the present price of around $67 and the moving averages near $60 reflects a period of sustained share-price strength relative to earlier in 2026. With the opening price on August 25 sitting nearly $6.53 above the 50-day moving average, Bristol-Myers Squibb stock has generated roughly double-digit percentage outperformance versus its own recent trend. For technical investors, this configuration can signal that momentum is firmly positive but also that the shares are more extended and could be sensitive to any disappointment in future earnings or pipeline updates.
Representative product: Zenbexus in multiple myeloma care
Within Bristol-Myers Squibb’s broad portfolio, Zenbexus (iberdomide) stands out as a representative product illustrating the company’s approach to targeted cancer therapies. As the first FDA-approved agent in the CELMoD class of molecular glue protein degraders, Zenbexus is designed to bind specific proteins and promote their degradation, thereby interrupting pathways that support multiple myeloma cell survival. The combination regimen approved by the FDA on August 13, 2026 incorporates Zenbexus alongside daratumumab, hyaluronidase-fihj and dexamethasone for adults who have already been treated with at least one proteasome inhibitor and one immunomodulatory agent but whose disease has relapsed.
Clinical data highlighted in scientific coverage indicate that the therapy delivered strong responses even in patients with prior exposure to multiple drug classes, leading to the accelerated approval based in part on minimal residual disease outcomes. This focus on residual disease underscores Bristol-Myers Squibb’s broader strategy of using advanced biomarkers and molecular diagnostics to refine oncology treatment and make drug approvals more directly tied to disease biology. Zenbexus therefore not only offers an additional option for relapsed multiple myeloma patients but also exemplifies the kind of high-innovation asset that can support the company’s earnings guidance and analyst confidence over the medium term.
Stock level and investor takeaway
As of the completed US session on August 24, 2026, Bristol-Myers Squibb stock closed at $67.28 on the New York Stock Exchange in US dollars, based on the cited real-time quote summary. Against FY 2026 EPS guidance of $6.75 to $7.00 and a consensus target of $66.06, the shares trade modestly above average analyst expectations but still on a forward earnings multiple under 10. Combined with the accelerated US approval of Zenbexus in mid-August 2026 and concentrated institutional ownership of 76.41 percent of outstanding shares, this leaves Bristol-Myers Squibb positioned as a large-cap biopharmaceutical name where valuation, pipeline innovation and professional investor support intersect in a relatively tight band around the high-$60s stock price.

Drugs & Therapies.content:
Share
Neuren Pharmaceuticals' partner Acadia Pharmaceuticals received European Commission marketing authorisation for DAYBUE (trofinetide) to treat Rett syndrome.
Neuren is entitled to receive US$35 million after the first commercial sale in Europe, alongside milestone payments up to US$170 million and tiered royalties.
The commercial rollout is expected to begin in Germany in early Q4 2026 to address neurobehavioural symptoms in Rett syndrome patients aged five and older.
Neuren Pharmaceuticals (ASX:NEU) secured European Commission marketing authorisation for DAYBUE (trofinetide) to treat neurobehavioural symptoms of Rett syndrome in adults and children aged five and older.
The approval expands DAYBUE as the first and only authorised treatment for Rett syndrome across all 27 European Union member states, as well as Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway.
"The European Commission’s approval of DAYBU is particularly rewarding for Neuren given our long-standing commitment to developing therapies for serious neurological disorders with profound unmet need," said Neuren CEO Jon Pilcher.
Under the licensing agreement, Neuren is eligible for up to US$170 million in potential sales milestone payments, plus tiered royalties ranging from mid-teen to low-20s percentage points of net sales.
Acadia Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ:ACAD) plans to initiate its initial European commercial launch in Germany in early Q4 2026.
Following the announcement, the Neuren share price was up at $22.68.
Neuren develops drug therapies for serious neurological disorders caused by genetic abnormalities or brain injury that currently lack approved treatment options.
The company's oral solution DAYBUE is already approved by regulatory authorities in the United States, Canada, and Israel, though it remains unapproved for sale in Australia.

Drugs & Therapies.url_match_title: One Center’s Oversized Impact on Drug Development and Clinical Trials - Tufts Now
Drugs & Therapies.content:
Some of the Center for the Study of Drug Development team, from left: Roula Krayem, senior research analyst; Kenneth Getz, executive director; Abby Dirks, senior data scientist; Sarah Wrobel, operations manager; Zak Smith, assistant director of data science and analytics; and Shailyn Bacchiocchi, communications coordinator.
 Photo: Courtesy of the CSDD
Healthcare
One Center’s Oversized Impact on Drug Development and Clinical Trials
Tufts Center for the Study of Drug Development celebrates 50 years of research and data publication to inform improvements in pharmaceutical development and regulatory policy
When pharmaceutical companies want to make their clinical trials faster and more efficient, they look at data compiled by the
Tufts Center for the Study of Drug Development
(CSDD). When the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) wants to know how the regulatory process affects drug development and approval times, they do the same. The U.S. Congress invites members of CSDD to testify. Clinical researchers consult publications from CSDD when designing and executing clinical trials. And when a layperson
reads an article
in the press about how much it costs to bring a new drug to market, it is CSDD that most likely provided the figure.
Since it was founded in 1976, CSDD has conducted scholarly analyses and published thousands of research articles that have helped pharmaceutical companies, regulatory agencies, and other research professionals in their ongoing efforts to improve the drug development process.
“We do large-scale empirical studies that we share as widely as possible with the drug development community,” said
Kenneth Getz
, research professor in the Public Health and Community Medicine Department at
Tufts University School of Medicine
and executive director of the center. “Our work helps the scientific and clinical research communities develop new treatments that address unmet and underserved medical needs faster and more efficiently.”
“The center has been a very reliable source of information about the trends in clinical research and how things are evolving,” said Robert Califf, a cardiologist at the Duke University School of Medicine who twice served as the commissioner of the FDA. “The information they produced was enormously helpful as the FDA thought about policy.”
Early Impacts
CSDD’s first impactful study, in the 1970s, documented that drugs were being approved in other major markets 3-7 years before the United States. At that time, for example, no beta blockers were available in the U.S. despite their widespread use in the United Kingdom for hypertension and other cardiovascular applications.
Ken Kaitin, then-associate director; Sheila Shulman, former assistant director; Joseph DiMasi, director of economic analysis; and Marilyn Gosse, former senior research fellow.
 Photo: Courtesy of Tufts Archival Research Center, taken by Brooks Kraft
“The FDA was seen as conservative and risk averse, and that study showed that U.S. citizens were paying a price: Important and sometimes life-saving therapeutic drugs were not reaching the market in a timely manner,” said
Kenneth Kaitin
, a professor at the School of Medicine who joined CSDD in 1986 and was director from 1997-2020. Kaitin said that “drug lag” study added fuel to the demands for regulatory reform of the FDA and led to congressional hearings.
When the FDA announced in the early 1990s that the drug lag had finally disappeared, the agency cited data from CSDD. According to Kaitin, that highlighted the philosophy of the center’s founder Louis Lasagna, that scholarly research and analyses can and should play an important role in informing public debate on drug development and policy.
Louis Lasagna, a renowned physician and pioneer in the field of clinical pharmacology, founded CSDD in 1976 at the University of Rochester with the goal of documenting information relating to the development and regulation of new medicines “to raise the intellectual level of debate on questions of public policy.” Lasagna brought the center with him when he joined Tufts University as the first dean of the
Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences
in 1984.
Another impactful study came in 1979, when the center showed that the cost to bring a drug to market was $54 million. Since then, the center has periodically updated this study, with the next report due out in the fall of 2026.
In 1983, the center showed that, due to lack of commercial incentives, the pharmaceutical industry tended to focus on the development of drugs for broad indications, leaving patients with rare diseases few options and little hope. That led to the passage of the
Orphan Drug Act
, which provides regulatory and commercial incentives for companies to develop drugs for rare diseases.
Expand
Louis Lasagna founded CSDD in 1976 at the University of Rochester and brought the center with him when he joined Tufts as the first dean of the Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences in 1984.
 Photo: Courtesy of Tufts Archival Research Center
Collapse modal
Louis Lasagna founded CSDD in 1976 at the University of Rochester and brought the center with him when he joined Tufts as the first dean of the Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences in 1984.
 Photo: Courtesy of Tufts Archival Research Center
The center also began a longitudinal study analyzing the success rate of drugs in clinical trials. Then, as now, the overwhelming majority of drugs and biologics fail to gain regulatory approval. “We’ve done a great deal of research helping to explain why drugs and biologics fail overall and by individual phases,” Getz said. “Many failed to demonstrate efficacy or had a poor safety profile. Others failed to enroll enough of the right patients or raised questions about clinical trial design and execution.”
“Our work helps the scientific and clinical research communities develop new treatments that address unmet and underserved medical needs faster and more efficiently.”
Share on Twitter
Digging Deeper
Since its founding, the center focused on documenting what Getz calls macro-level issues, such as development costs and timelines. About 20 years ago, the center added a series of studies to get a clearer picture of underlying factors behind some of those big trends. “Protocol design and execution is one of the largest, if not the largest, drivers of rising costs and increasing levels of inefficiencies and longer timelines,” Getz said.
Every five years, Getz leads a study to analyze clinical trial protocols, which includes, among other things, quantifying the type and number of endpoints, procedures supporting them, and the number of data points generated. He has found that protocols are becoming ever more scientifically and operationally complex with highly customized designs requiring more elaborate and demanding logistics to administer.
“Complexity is running away from us,” he said. “In 2012, [the average protocol collected] under a million data points and today it’s more than 6 million as pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies focus on more challenging diseases, target more narrowly defined patient communities, and execute more global and more expansive clinical trial activity.”
Expand
Every five years, Kenneth Getz leads a study to analyze clinical trial protocols, which includes, among other things, quantifying the type and number of endpoints, procedures supporting them, and the number of data points generated.
 Photo: Courtesy of Kenneth Getz
Collapse modal
Every five years, Kenneth Getz leads a study to analyze clinical trial protocols, which includes, among other things, quantifying the type and number of endpoints, procedures supporting them, and the number of data points generated.
 Photo: Courtesy of Kenneth Getz
While each clinical trial protocol is unique, Getz said it’s possible to identify common areas for improvement. “We devised a methodology to characterize certain design decisions,” he said, “and found there are a lot of areas that could be simplified.” One such area is the proliferation of patient procedures that don’t directly inform the primary endpoint the trial is measuring.
Including too many procedures not only takes more time and money, it can also deter potential participants. Indeed, the center is finding that recruitment and retention are increasing challenges.
Mary Jo Lamberti
, research associate professor at the School of Medicine and director of sponsored research at CSDD, hopes her work might help change that. “The more patients who can participate in trials, the more chances we have of getting treatments for some of the more difficult-to-treat diseases like Alzheimer’s disease or certain forms of cancer or rare diseases,” she said. “That’s how I became interested in this work. We identify areas of inefficiency and gather valuable benchmark data and generate insights.”
Lamberti gathers and publishes data related to recruitment and retention trends. She is seeing companies broaden their reach to include more sites and screen more potential study participants for a trial.
She also collects data on new tactics companies are using to reach and recruit patients, such as using artificial intelligence to seek potential participants through electronic health records and using chatbots to engage with participants.
The Center for the Study of Drug Development team. Back row, from left: Sarah Wrobel, operations manager; Mary Jo Lamberti, director of sponsored research; Abby Dirks, senior data scientist; Zak Smith, assistant director of data science and analytics; Joseph DiMasi, director of economic analysis; Maria Florez, senior consultant; Jennifer Kim, research associate professor. Front row, from left: Emily Botto, former senior research analyst; Hana Do, research analyst; Madison Ford, research analyst; Kenneth Getz, executive director; Ava Feuer, former communications coordinator; and Victoria Zhang, intern.
 Photo: Courtesy of the CSDD
Reducing Complexity and Burden
Zak Smith
, assistant director of data science and analytics at CSDD, evaluates strategies intended to streamline complex protocols, such as decentralized clinical trials (DCT). DCT refers to a collection of techniques and technologies to reduce visits to the research site, including telehealth visits, wearable data-collecting devices, mobile clinics, and allowing participants to complete procedures close to home.
“One of the things we’ve seen that can have the biggest impact on trial performance is to allow patients to get procedures or lab tests done with their primary care physician or at a local lab rather than visiting the clinical trial site,” he said. “That’s one of the easier and more straightforward ways to ease the burden on the participant’s side.”
He has also looked to see whether DCT strategies improve proportional representation in trials – that is, making sure the demographics of participants matches that of the intended population. “We saw that some DCT solutions may help improve diversity and others are associated with less,” he said. “Allowing the use of local labs was associated with increased diversity within the clinical trials.”
Smith has also developed a way to quantify how burdensome it is to participate in clinical trials. He analyzed thousands of patient surveys about the perceived burden of procedures and other common requirements of clinical trials. He uses the results to assess draft protocols that companies submit.
“We break it down into individual procedures, calculate a burden score and say, ‘Your burden is higher or lower than our benchmark,’” he said. “It always sparks some great conversations between the companies and us.”
“The more patients who can participate in trials, the more chances we have of getting treatments for some of the more difficult-to-treat diseases like Alzheimer’s disease or certain forms of cancer or rare diseases.”
Share on Twitter
Supporting Change
Moving forward, Getz wants the center to focus even more on data that could help organizations manage change in this era when everything seems to be moving at lightning speed, most notably AI.
To that end, he brought on
Jennifer Kim
, research associate professor at the School of Medicine, who is the first member of CSDD with a Ph.D. in behavioral science. “I came on board to look at drug development using a people-centered approach,” she said. “I’ve always been interested in understanding ways to tie the study of human behavior and organizational performance optimization, and in this case, we’re looking at optimizing drug development through human behavior.”
Kim is investigating the readiness of both organizations and individuals to respond to the changes that are happening in drug development. “We are looking at organizational changes, including how people are responding to AI being incorporated into their workflow, the resistance to that, and ways to address that resistance,” she said.
Seated, from left: Sheila Shulman, Louis Lasagna, Kenneth Kaitin. Standing, from left: Joseph DiMasi, Marilyn Gosse, Brenda McGinnis, Toni Snow, Jeffrey Brown, Essie Mack-Pack, Mark Seibring, Peg Hewitt, Michael Manocchia.
 Photo: Courtesy of the CSDD
On the participant side, she’s studied how participants’ interactions with research staff influence their satisfaction with the experience and their willingness to complete the clinical trial and participate in future research. She found that those interactions carry a lot of weight. That’s significant, she said, because improving those interactions could be an easy-to-implement strategy to increase retention and even grow the population of future participants.
“We want patients of all backgrounds to have a good experience and to be able to go into their community and tell family and friends that participating in clinical trials is safe and can be life-enhancing,” she said.
While Kim’s work represents a new direction for the center, Getz said the longitudinal studies documenting cost, timelines, and success rates will continue. “Organizations follow these longitudinal studies to monitor how practices and use of solutions are impacting drug development performance,” he said. “There is no shortage of work to do there. At the same time, CSDD is moving into new domains. The drug development community started demanding more actionable and practical ways to react to insights we were offering, so we are evolving.”
No matter what the future brings, Getz remains committed to the mission. “I’m passionate about collecting hard data and evidence to inform insights,” he said. “We have amazing people at CSDD who share that same passion, and we love to watch the impact our research has on drug development strategies, practices, and performance. It’s meaningful and consequential work.”

US Approves First Drug That Targets Root Cause of Narcolepsy Rather Than...
A Japanese pharma company has developed a drug that treats the root cause of a leading form of narcolepsy, and is celebrating as it becomes the first of its kind to receive American FDA approval.
Narcolepsy type-1 afflicts 120,000 people in the US, and is characterized by sudden bouts of intense daytime drowsiness, disrupted nighttime sleep, and cataplexy, or sudden muscle weakness while awake
Traditionally treated by simulants to stay awake, or nervous system depressants to dampen cataplexy, this new drug mimics the body’s production of orexin, a compound that helps regulate wakefulness that is disrupted in patients with narcolepsy.
Called Orzeyful, it’s been developed by Takeda, and Tiffany Farchione, MD, Director of the FDA’s Division of Psychiatry, celebrated its approval in an August 5th
statement
.
“For too long, people with narcolepsy type 1 have had to manage a complex, lifelong neuropsychiatric condition with treatments that only address pieces of it,” said Farchione. “This new drug is the first medicine that impacts the underlying biology of the disease, treating narcolepsy type 1 as a whole.”
Its developers likewise celebrated the milestone.
“The FDA approval of Orzeyful marks a new chapter for the narcolepsy type 1 community, as we introduce an entirely new class of medicine that will potentially redefine how this disease is managed and how people feel on treatment,” says Takeda president and CEO Julie Kim in a separate
statement
.
The final stage trials that paved the way for approval demonstrated safety and efficacy in 273 patients. Compared to placebo, those who took the twice-daily pill for 12 weeks were able to stay awake longer during the day and rest better at night.
“It’s the best thing that has ever happened to me,” Tyler Chapman, who participated in one of the clinical trials, told Nature’s in-house press publication. “My quality of life is so much better.”
NEW THERAPEUTICS:
New Kind of Antibiotic Is First in 30 Years to Treat UTIs That Keep Coming Back
There were side effects, including of a severity that saw some participants removed from the trial. The most common serious side effects were increased frequency and urgency to urinate, and—ironically—insomnia. Nevertheless the side effect occurrence was considered low.
Orexin, the chemical signaling molecule produced by brain cells which die in narcolepsy type-1, has been linked to other neurological conditions like ADHD, and even Parkinson’s, and with Orzeyful’s FDA approval comes the potential for future research into its utility as a neuro-modulator.
ALSO CHECK OUT:
New Drug Could Change Lives of Kids with Resistant Epilepsy, Patient Trials Concluded
“Orzeyful is just the beginning. With orexin emerging as a powerful therapeutic pathway, Takeda is unlocking the potential of this new class of medicine for patients across a range of disorders,” says Andy Plump, the company’s president of research and development, in also the statement.

Anti obesity drug approved in UK to ease hunger, promote weight loss
Developer plans to work with NHS to get therapy to aHO patients 4 and older
Written by
Marisa Horak MS
|
Aug. 24, 2026
Share
Share this page with email
Share this page on Facebook
Share this page on X
Share this page on Reddit
Print
Preferred Source on Google
Imcivree is an anti obesity drug designed to curb hunger and help patients lose weight. (Image by iStock)
Imcivree
(setmelanotide), Rhythm Pharmaceuticals’ anti obesity drug, is now approved in the United Kingdom to help promote weight loss and control hunger in people as young as age 4 with
acquired hypothalamic obesity
(aHO).
The U.K.’s Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has expanded the drug’s marketing authorization to include aHO, Rhythm announced in a
company press release
. That decision adds the rare disorder, which can develop after damage to a brain area called the hypothalamus, to the list of approved uses of Imcivree in the U.K.
“Patients with acquired HO often experience persistent hunger and rapid, severe weight gain that can affect nearly every aspect of their daily life,” said David Meeker, MD, chairman, president and CEO of
Rhythm
.
According to Meeker, this approval “marks an important milestone for patients in the UK living with acquired HO.”
The therapy had already been cleared by the MHRA to manage obesity and control hunger in people with certain genetic conditions affecting hunger regulation in the brain. That includes
Bardet-Biedl syndrome
, an inherited multisystemic disorder that can also lead to obesity.
Rhythm said it would be working closely with the U.K.’s National Health Service (NHS) to finalize plans for coverage of Imcivree in people with aHO.
“With the MHRA’s expanded authorization of IMCIVREE, healthcare providers now have an approved treatment option for eligible patients that addresses the underlying biology of [aHO],” Meeker said.
Recommended Reading
Aug. 10, 2026
News
by
Marisa Horak MS
New treatment for acquired obesity sees strong early US uptake
The decision in the U.K. follows similar expansion approvals of Imcivree to treat aHO in the
U.S.
and the
European Union
.
Rhythm granted 10 years’ market exclusivity for Imcivree
In addition, the therapy was awarded orphan drug status by the MHRA for aHO, according to Rhythm. That designation provides reductions on marketing authorization fees and a market exclusivity of 10 years in Great Britain.
aHO is marked by damage to a part of the brain called the hypothalamus, which serves much like a master switch for keeping the body balanced. Normally, this brain region can activate the melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) signaling pathway, which is helps regulate appetite. Imcivree, administered via a once-daily injection, is designed to activate this pathway, thereby restoring normal signaling to regulate hunger.
“Acquired hypothalamic obesity is a complex condition that can have profound effects on the quality of life and long-term health of children and adults with brain tumors affecting the hypothalamus,” said Sadaf Farooqi, MD, PhD, of the University of Cambridge in the U.K.
The TRANSCEND study showed substantial reductions in BMI in adults and children, demonstrating the effectiveness of [this] pathway-targeted therapy in people with [aHO].
The MHRA’s approval of Imcivree for aHO was based largely on data from the global
Phase 3 TRANSCEND clinical trial (NCT05774756)
, which tested Imcivree against a placebo in more than 100 people with aHO. The goal was to evaluate the therapy’s effect on body mass index (BMI), which is a ratio of weight to height commonly used as a proxy of body fat.
After one year, average BMI
decreased by 17%
with Imcivree and increased by 3% with the placebo, meeting the trial’s main goal. Also, more than three-quarters of participants given Imcivree experienced a BMI reduction of 5% or more compared with less than one-quarter of those on the placebo (83% vs. 21%).
Data from TRANSCEND also indicated that Imcivree helped reduce patient-reported hunger. The most commonly reported adverse events with the therapy were nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, injection site reaction, skin darkening, and headache.
“The TRANSCEND study showed substantial reductions in BMI in adults and children, demonstrating the effectiveness of MC4R pathway-targeted therapy in people with this condition,” Farooqi said. “These results provide strong evidence for a targeted treatment approach in a condition for which there were previously no approved therapies in the UK.”

Drugs & Therapies.content:
logo
-- Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient Facility Validated for Global Commercial Manufacturing
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. Aug. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire=YONHAP/ -- Cambrex, a leading global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO), today announced the successful completion of three Pre-Approval Inspections (PAIs) at its High Point, North Carolina facility by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Japan's Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA), and Australia's Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA). The completion of all three inspections enables High Point to manufacture approved active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) for the United States, Japan, and Australia, establishing the facility as the newest commercial manufacturing site within the Cambrex global network.
PAIs are conducted by regulatory agencies to assess a facility's quality systems, manufacturing processes, data integrity, and operational controls before commercial products can be approved for manufacture at the site.
The milestone follows Cambrex's $38 million expansion of the High Point facility completed in 2023, which added analytical and chemical development laboratories, clinical manufacturing suites, and commercial manufacturing operations with reactors up to 2,000 liters. The site is designed to support lower-volume commercial products, including orphan drugs, precision medicines, and other specialized therapies serving smaller patient populations.
"Successfully completing these inspections demonstrates the strength of our quality systems and the dedication of the High Point team," said Thomas Loewald, Chief Executive Officer, Cambrex. "As more therapies are developed for targeted patient populations, the industry increasingly requires commercial manufacturing capacity at smaller scales. High Point was purpose-built to meet that need, providing customers with an efficient and flexible path from development to long-term commercial supply."
High Point complements Cambrex's global development and manufacturing network by providing customers with a seamless path from process development and clinical manufacturing through commercial production. The addition of commercial manufacturing capabilities in North Carolina further expands the company's ability to support customer programs throughout the product lifecycle.
About Cambrex
Cambrex is a leading global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) that provides drug substance development and manufacturing across the entire drug lifecycle, as well as comprehensive analytical services.
With over 45 years of experience and a team of 2,000 experts servicing global clients from North America and Europe, Cambrex offers a range of specialized drug substance technologies and capabilities, including continuous flow, controlled substances, peptide synthesis, solid-state science, biocatalysis, material characterization, complex synthetics, and highly potent APIs.
Source: Cambrex
